rules.statement: In a test project, when code compares a size threshold in bytes for a generic element type (for example `count * Unsafe.SizeOf<T>()` against a page size), test the boundary on both sides with an element type larger than one byte, not only with `byte`.
rules.why: If only `byte` is tested, element count and byte count are the same number. A regression that counts elements instead of bytes would then pass every test while handing callers buffers that are too short for wider types.
rules.check: Look for new or changed size or threshold logic that multiplies by `Unsafe.SizeOf<T>()` or `sizeof(T)`. Confirm that some test uses a wider T (such as `int` or `char`) and asserts the result at exactly threshold/sizeof(T) elements and at one element more.
